key_insight: GaOx can act as a conductive hole transport layer for 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cells when formed by ion exchange during absorber co-evaporation, enabling strong passivation and high VOC.
engineering_relevance: This points to a simpler, low-additive back-contact design for tandem-ready chalcopyrite bottom cells with improved voltage and >16% active-area efficiency.
method: Formed GaOx during co-evaporation of the low-bandgap CuInSe2 absorber.
Tested whether Cu addition, Na, and oxygen-flow conditions affect GaOx conductivity.
Examined microstructure and device performance of the passivating back-contact stack.
evidence_signal: The optimized device reached above 16% active-area efficiency and a record-certified VOC of 552 mV.
watch_item: The conductive GaOx appears condition-dependent and partly crystalline, so transfer to other fabrication routes or contact stacks may require careful process control.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
